detail.abstract: This study examines how detracking affects student achievement by analyzing the 2013 expansion of South Korea's High School Equalization Policy (EP), which replaced exam-based admissions with residence-based assignment and substantially increased classroom heterogeneity. Using both administrative achievement data from the National Assessment of Educational Achievement and large-scale student survey data, we evaluate the academic and behavioral consequences of equalizing peer composition. Employing a synthetic difference-indifferences estimator, we find that equalizing peer composition lowered average test scores on average by 0.08 to 0.1 standard deviations across core subjects. Distributional analyses show that the decline is concentrated among high-performing students, while the share of mid-and low-performing students remains unchanged. Further analysis reveals that the EP led to significant reductions in students' self-reported class preparation and in their perceptions of peers' study effort. The results highlight the central role of peer composition in the education production function and underscore the need for complementary pedagogical support when implementing equalization reforms.

detail.abstract: The Forecast Value Added (FVA) literature documents that human adjustments to statistical forecasts frequently degrade accuracy, attributing this to cognitive biases. We propose an important extension: some harmful adjustments may reflect intentional strategic manipulation rather than unintentional cognitive error. When performance pressures create misaligned incentives, forecasting analysts-serving as epistemic gatekeepers-may strategically manipulate forecasts or accuracy metrics to optimize personal performance rather than organizational decision quality. We develop a dual-pathway framework distinguishing cognitive errors (unintentional, from information processing limitations) from strategic gaming (intentional, driven by incentive misalignment). This distinction has profound practical implications: cognitive errors require debiasing interventions, while strategic gaming requires governance solutions. Misdiagnosing strategic behavior as cognitive error leads to ineffective interventions. This paper is conceptual rather than empirical. We argue that theory predicts strategic manipulation could occur under identifiable conditions, and that this possibility warrants systematic empirical investigation.

title: Non-Quantifiable Exploitation: From Unpaid Female Emotional Labor to Boundaryless Corporate Demands in Post-Capitalist China
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Non-Quantifiable Exploitation: From Unpaid Female Emotional Labor to Boundaryless Corporate Demands in Post-Capitalist China
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of “non-quantifiable exploitation”—a mode of extraction that operates without measurable standards, boundaries, or compensation. Originating in the unpaid emotional and cognitive labor historically imposed on women, the same logic has migrated into contemporary Chinese corporate culture through 24/7 availability expectations and mandatory affective performance. Unlike Marxian surplus-value extraction, non-quantifiable exploitation relies on internalized self-discipline rather than formal coercion, making it extremely sticky yet brittle once legitimacy collapses. Evidence from feminist awakenings in Japan and anti-involution movements in China illustrates the explosive potential of reclaimed energy when the internalized obligation structure fractures.

title: Primordial Precedent: Why All Human Territorial Disputes Are Geologically Frivolous
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Primordial Precedent: Why All Human Territorial Disputes Are Geologically Frivolous
detail.abstract:
This commentary challenges the foundational legitimacy of human territorial sovereignty through a novel, geological-legal lens. It posits that the original and continuous title to Earth is held by the prokaryotic descendants of LUCA (the Last Universal Common Ancestor), whose 3.5-billion-year stewardship constitutes a primordial freehold. The subsequent 165-million-year tenancy of the Dinosauria further establishes a precedent that renders modern human claims frivolous.

The article argues that human nation-states are merely temporary tenants, guilty of breach of covenant (ecological destruction), nuisance (borders), and frivolous litigation (territorial disputes). Framed as a legal submission on behalf of these primordial entities, the commentary culminates in a proposed "Prokaryotic & Saurian Sovereignty Act" (P.S.S.A.), which formally subordinates human sovereignty to these ancient claims. The work serves as a polemic call for humility, urging humanity to recognize its fleeting and destructive tenancy within the context of Deep Time.

detail.abstract:
This study analyzes how trade unionism in Argentina confronts automation and artificial intelligence. The author argues that technology is not a neutral process, but rather a field of dispute where power relations are being redefined. Argentina, with its rich history of labor organizing, serves as a key case study for observing how traditional institutions face a digital revolution that threatens to fragment labor.

The research highlights that digitalization has an unequal impact. While transitions are being negotiated in the banking sector, extreme precarity is observed in the platform economy. Here, algorithmic management acts as an invisible boss that evades legal responsibilities, isolating the worker and breaking down historical bonds of solidarity.

To avoid becoming obsolete, unions must move from defensive resistance to a proactive approach. This involves using collective bargaining to demand data transparency and ongoing training. The text concludes that only ethical governance and tripartite dialogue between the state, businesses, and unions will allow productivity to translate into social progress, ensuring that technology is a tool for human dignity and not an engine of inequality.

title: From Zero-Sum to Shared Symbol: Reimagining Sovereignty through the 'Jerusalem' State Model
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Zero-Sum to Shared Symbol: Reimagining Sovereignty through the 'Jerusalem' State Model
detail.abstract: This commentary proposes a radical symbolic solution to break the intractable Israeli-Palestinian deadlock. It argues that the conflict is trapped in a "war of symbols," where the very names "Israel" and "Palestine" represent mutually exclusive national narratives, making territorial compromise feel like a betrayal of identity. The article contends that the current paradigm is designed to fail and that a breakthrough requires surrendering these exclusive national names in favor of a shared, higher identity. The proposed solution is the establishment of a binational state formally named the Jerusalem Republic. This strategic inversion transforms Jerusalem from a contested prize into a shared legacy, fostering a new civic identity as "citizens of Jerusalem." For its governance, the paper adapts the model of asymmetric autonomy, drawing on Indonesia's Special Region of Yogyakarta. It suggests designating the physical city as the Special Administrative Region of Jerusalem—a shared capital with a power-sharing council to guarantee the rights and holy sites of all communities. The commentary concludes that while this vision demands the profound sacrifice of sovereign naming, it offers a path to end zero-sum conflict, secure a shared capital, and liberate both peoples from the burden of perpetual strife. It serves as a normative framework to make the unimaginable imaginable and reorient the pursuit of peace from borders to a common, symbolic foundation.

detail.abstract: Ramon Ontiveros' conspiracy to defraud the United States is not an anomaly, it is a lesson learned from a system built to look away. This essay examines how Ontiveros' actions reveal deeper failures within the U.S. immigration and labor structures: a culture that rewards coercion, punishes vulnerability, and turns immigrant fear into an economic resource. Rather than treating the immigration system as "broken," this work asks a more urgent question: what if the system is functioning exactly as designed? What if its inefficiencies, contradictions, and abuses are not errors, but features? Through political reflection, philosophical analysis, and firsthand insight into coercion, retaliation, and institutional silence, this essay confronts the uncomfortable possibility that exploitation in America is not an accident, it is an expectation.

title: Add-On Pricing under Consumer Valuation Uncertainty
affiliations: A.B. Freeman School of Business, Tulane University, University of Science and Technology of China - School of Management,  and University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration

detail.title: Add-On Pricing under Consumer Valuation Uncertainty
detail.abstract:
Problem definition:
Three add-on pricing strategies are prevalent in practice: pure bundling (bundle), unbundling (base good and add-on), and mixed bundling (base good, add-on, and bundle). In many situations, the purchase time of the base good (e.g., hotel room) is separated from the consumption time of the add-on (e.g., breakfast), often leading to consumer valuation uncertainty about the add-on when purchasing the base good. In addition, the add-on in a bundle can be delivered either at the purchase time of the base good (i.e., add-on product) or at its consumption time (i.e., add-on service), yielding different cost structures. This paper examines the optimal add-on pricing strategy to exploit consumer valuation uncertainty in both monopoly and duopoly competition for different types of add-on goods.

Methodology/Results:
In a game-theoretic model, we first characterize the market conditions for each pricing strategy (i.e., pure bundling, unbundling, and mixed bundling) to be optimal. This is in stark contrast to prior literature on add-on pricing which usually ignores mixed bundling. Under mixed bundling, consumers with a high expected valuation purchase the add-on up front at a discount with valuation uncertainty, whereas consumers with a low expected valuation wait until the uncertainty is resolved but at a higher price. Second, we show that competition in general makes pure bundling more likely to be adopted. Third, the cost structure of the add-on good---whether its cost depends on the consumption state---plays a significant role. One of the novel findings is that for add-on service with state-dependent costs, unbundling is never optimal.

Managerial implications:
This paper provides novel managerial insights for add-on pricing as a price discrimination device to exploit consumer valuation uncertainty. When determining the optimal add-on pricing strategy, firms should take into account the heterogeneity of consumer valuation uncertainty, the cost structure of add-on, and competition intensity.

detail.title: Public service reformation: Relationship building by mobile technology
detail.abstract: Extensive implementation of information and communication technology (ICT) in public administration has created the capacity to reengineer public service systems to develop a new service delivery channel using the continuous interactivity of the mobile phone's short messaging service (SMS). An empirical study was conducted among general citizens in Bangladesh, who are the actual users of public service. The study revealed that the critical factors which contribute to the development of attitude toward public administration for service delivery through mobile phone SMS are: time and location, relevance, and reliability.

title: Digital Resilience in Crisis: How Bangladesh’s Information Technology Sector Weathered the COVID-19 Storm ​
affiliations: United International University and United International University

detail.title: Digital Resilience in Crisis: How Bangladesh’s Information Technology Sector Weathered the COVID-19 Storm ​
detail.abstract: The IT sector in Bangladesh has been expanding over the decades, but its ability to withstand systemic shocks was never tested until the COVID-19 pandemic. This paper assesses the potential for significant changes in industry performance between the pre-COVID period (FY2018-FY2020) and the post-COVID period (FY2021-FY2023), thereby examining the digital resilience of an emerging economy. Paired-sample t-tests and correlation matrices were analysed DSE-listed Bangladeshi IT companies across eight key financial ratios. Despite the negative effects of COVID-19, the IT sector has performed remarkably well due to increased demand for online-based business operations. Moreover, business owners relied more on online interactions because of social distancing measures. The liquidity, activity, and profitability demonstrate the industry’s notable stability in operations and profits. On the other hand, the industry focused on leveraging resources to ensure uninterrupted operations and seized opportunities during COVID-19. However, increasing leverage could cause long-term stress unless strategic decisions are made to sustain growth. Overall, Bangladesh’s IT sector exhibited strong liquidity, operational resilience, and profitability, although solvency pressures increased due to higher debt. The findings highlight the sector’s adaptive capacity and economic contribution during the global crisis, emphasizing the importance of careful leverage policies to maintain growth after the crisis.

title: Management – The Researcher View
affiliations: Vivekananda Institute of Professional Studies-Technical Campus

detail.title: Management – The Researcher View
detail.abstract: The Indian corporate governance code is based on the Anglo-Saxon model of which suitability has been questioned by various experts arguing that India needs to develop its own corporate governance code because business groups – business families and the government --dominate the Indian corporate sector unlike the corporate sectors in the USA and UK, where concentration of shareholding is less eminent and shares are widely held by geographically dispersed investors. In this paper researcher argue that asking ‘what is the best corporate governance model’ is futile. Rather, countries develop corporate governance models that fit their legal, institutions, political circumstances, and position in the global economy. Moreover, convergence is unlikely because any process of change, whether induced by globalization or not, takes place in a political context. Study proposes to intensify research efforts on cross-national patterns of corporate governance from a comparative approach that takes national diversity and its consequences seriously into account.

title: Digital Marketing Credentials in Business Education: Boosting Workforce Relevance
affiliations: Point Loma Nazarene University, Saint Francis University,  and Brock University

detail.title: Digital Marketing Credentials in Business Education: Boosting Workforce Relevance
detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has reshaped marketing practice and marketing education. Modern graduates need both foundational marketing knowledge and technical skills, often verified by industry certifications and micro-credentials. These credentials validate skills, improve employability, and motivate students through hands on learning experiences that foster a deeper understanding of the subject matter. Yet, their impact is limited by inconsistent integration and faculty engagement. This paper argues that digital marketing certifications and badges should be strategically integrated into marketing curricula, informed by educational theory and workplace needs, to maximize their value and impact.

title: The Move to Opportunity for Vocational Experience Act (MOVE Act)
affiliations: The University of Texas School of Law

detail.title: The Move to Opportunity for Vocational Experience Act (MOVE Act)
detail.abstract: The Move to Opportunity for Vocational Experience Act (MOVE Act) establishes a federal mobility-support program designed to address growing geographic mismatches in the U.S. labor market, particularly as AI-driven economic change makes the location of high-demand jobs increasingly unpredictable. The Act directs the Department of Labor to create a national, vetted list of employment and registered apprenticeship opportunities that offer documented economic security and are located in communities with the capacity to support incoming workers. Eligible participants who accept these MOVE opportunities receive a $10,000 relocation grant, adjusted annually for inflation, to offset upfront moving costs that often prevent workers from accessing higher-quality labor market matches. The program pairs this support with an income-contingent repayment mechanism—requiring participants to remit 2 percent of their income for five years, capped at the grant amount—which avoids traditional debt burdens while aligning repayment with realized earnings. To ensure accuracy and accountability, hosts (state and local economic development entities or industry associations) must demonstrate sustained demand for listed roles and may be required to partially reimburse the federal government if participants cannot secure employment despite good-faith efforts. The Act also mandates significant data collection, program evaluation, and privacy protections to assess outcomes and inform congressional review. Overall, the MOVE Act represents a novel federal intervention that seeks to enhance labor mobility, improve matching efficiency, and strengthen regional economies in an era of rapid technological and geographic labor market restructuring.

title: Editors' Introduction: Artificial Intelligence and Strategy—Charting New Frontiers
affiliations: University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business and University of Southern California - Marshall School of Business

detail.title: Editors' Introduction: Artificial Intelligence and Strategy—Charting New Frontiers
detail.abstract: We introduce this handbook as a collective exploration of how artificial intelligence reshapes the foundations and practice of strategic management. The chapters that follow are organized around four themes—Theories, Tools, Teaching, and Terrains—revisiting foundational constructs while introducing fresh concepts such as fusion skills, algorithmic ambidexterity, and AI surprises. Written by leading scholars in early 2025, these chapters explore nascent ideas and speculate about emerging trajectories in a rapidly evolving field. We address three audiences: researchers developing new theoretical frameworks, educators redesigning curricula and pedagogy, and practitioners seeking research-backed guidance for deploying AI responsibly. Each chapter provides actionable takeaways while examining how AI transforms both firms’ external competitive strategies and their internal processes of learning, decision-making, and governance. Together, these contributions capture the field’s best conjectures at a moment of profound technological change. Our hope is that this volume will serve as a catalyst for the next generation of research on AI and strategy.

title: Translational AI: A New Discipline for Turning Model Potential into Market Success
affiliations: Department of Computer Science, School of Engineering & Computer Science, Baylor University

detail.title: Translational AI: A New Discipline for Turning Model Potential into Market Success
detail.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence into the enterprise faces a critical dissonance: despite billions in capital allocation, initiatives frequently succumb to the Green Dashboard Paradox, where technical metrics signal health immediately prior to catastrophic business failure. We argue this stems from a fundamental category error in management philosophy: the application of deterministic control frameworks to govern probabilistic, evolving AI agents. This mismatch creates a "translation gap" that decouples model performance from economic utility. To bridge this divide, we propose Translational AI (TAI), a new management discipline that synthesizes strategic framing, socio-technical system design, and adaptive stewardship. Drawing on game theoretic dynamics specifically Akerlof's Adverse Selection and the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma, we demonstrate how current market incentives trap firms in structural dysfunction, forcing rational actors into a "race to the bottom" or a "market for lemons." We conclude by providing a mechanism design framework for institutionalizing TAI specifically through the Variance Audit and Cognitive Dividend-enabling leaders to escape these traps and convert raw algorithmic potential into sustainable competitive advantage.

title: Crude oil price hikes and exchange rate volatility: A lesson from the Bangladesh economy
affiliations: East West University, University of Otago and National University, Bangladesh

detail.title: Crude oil price hikes and exchange rate volatility: A lesson from the Bangladesh economy
detail.abstract: Crude oil price volatility has drawn greater concern for the prudent exchange rate policy as well as price stability. Net oil-importing countries, like Bangladesh, experience persistent currency devaluation due to the oil price volatility in the international market. Understanding the relationship between oil price and exchange rate nexus, this study examines the oil price and exchange rate volatility by using daily time series data from 2015 to 2023. Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity (GARCH) and exponential GARCH (EGARCH) models have been used to analyze the effects of oil price shocks on the nominal exchange rate. According to the study, a rise in oil prices leads to a depreciation of Bangladesh's taka vis-à-vis the US dollar. The study also shows that oil price shocks have a long-lasting impact on exchange rate volatility, and the shocks to exchange rate volatility have an asymmetric effect, implying that the negative shocks give rise to higher volatility of exchange rates than positive shocks. This is an original study that contributes to the research gap by explaining the nexus between oil price and exchange rates.

title: Cognitive Uncertainty across Humans and Large Language Models: Regard and Recall in Economic Decision Making

detail.title: Cognitive Uncertainty across Humans and Large Language Models: Regard and Recall in Economic Decision Making
detail.abstract: This paper studies when, and along which dimensions, large language models (LLMs) can substitute for humans in normative economic decision tasks. Building on the cognitive uncertainty (CU) framework of Enke et al., I construct a joint human-LLM dataset that places GPT-4 and experimental subjects on an identical item bank of belief-updating, risk, and expectations problems. Decision complexity is decomposed into four channels-probability structure, search difficulty, representation difficulty, and steps required-and both humans and the LLM report decision-level CU, interpreted as the subjective probability that their answer lies within a domain-appropriate accuracy band. I estimate how CU varies with these channels and with representational form. The LLM is substantially more accurate and roughly 20 percentage points more confident than humans on the same tasks, but the CU profiles differ sharply: human CU is tightly tuned to complex probabilities and, more modestly, to search depth, while LLM CU is largely insensitive to those dimensions and instead declines with symbolic contortion and step depth. These patterns suggest that cognitive uncertainty traces distinct "cognitive taxes" on regard-based and recall-based expertise, implying that human-LLM substitution will be domain-specific and that hybrid arrangements may be most valuable where their respective vulnerability profiles are complementary.

detail.abstract: Value relevance of financial statement has been in research for academics over the last four decades. While there has been a number of studies on the value relevance in the developed countries such as the US and UK, but very few empirical study was conducted in developing markets. Therefore, the aim of this study is to examine the value relevance of financial reporting and its impact on stock price. In order to achieve this goal, a model that includes six specific financial ratios has been developed. The sample data of 127 non-financial companies listed on HOSE, is collected primarily from their financial statements and other credible sources in the time fames spans of 2008 - 2013. The results reveal that inventories to sales ratio, working capital to total assets ratio have a negative impact on stock return, while the ratio of net profit to total assets and net profit to sales ratio affect stock price movement positively.

title: More Than Human: The Informational Effects of AI-Powered Corporate Disclosure
affiliations: Georgia State University - Robinson College of Business and Peking University HSBC Business School

detail.title: More Than Human: The Informational Effects of AI-Powered Corporate Disclosure
detail.abstract: We examine firms’ use of AI to help generate the language in their corporate disclosures. Employing state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) to detect and quantify AI-generated content in earnings conference calls during 2015-2024, we find that AI-powered disclosure is widespread and increasingly prevalent across firms and industries. AI-generated language exhibits relatively more positive sentiment and greater linguistic sophistication, yet it does not appear to help managers strategically mislead investors. Indeed, managers who have stronger incentives to opportunistically distort market perceptions tend to rely less on AI-generated text. We also find that AI-powered disclosure is associated with larger stock market responses to earnings releases, tighter bid-ask spreads, and smaller analyst forecast errors. These informational benefits are greater when the CEO has a personal linguistic style characterized by less clarity or more tonal inconsistency. The results from instrumental variables regressions suggest that the positive associations between AI-generated language and disclosure informativeness are causal. Overall, we conclude that AI is an important tool for enhancing the quality of corporate disclosures to market participants.

title: The Regional Economic Impact of Weather Shocks: Evidence from Portugal
affiliations: Nova School of Business and Economics, NOVA University Lisbon - NOVA Information Management School (NOVA IMS) and Nova School of Business and Economics

detail.title: The Regional Economic Impact of Weather Shocks: Evidence from Portugal
detail.abstract: Weather extremes play an important role in shaping short-run economic activity, yet the literature offers little evidence on how weather shocks translate into household spending. This study examines the short-term economic impacts of temperature, wildfire risk, and a novel measure of rainfall volatility on point-of sales purchases, unemployment, and housing prices using a panel of Portuguese municipalities from 2010 to 2021. A panel vector autoregressive model with exogenous variables including cross-border spillovers from similar climate regimes using climate factors as controls is used. Panel local projections show that a one-standard-deviation increase in hourly rainfall volatility raises purchases and house-price growth, and lowers unemployment. Increases in mean temperature boost spending, whereas temperature variability dampens it, and wildfire risk reduces consumption.  Introducing disposable income, non-linear terms, longer lags, or event-count weather indicators leaves these elasticities virtually unchanged.  Regional analyses reveal that responses in the Lisbon Metropolitan Area and Algarve (southern Portugal) are not only larger but sometimes opposite in direction compared to those in northern Portugal. To the best of our knowledge, the findings provide the first evidence of weather-induced fluctuations in purchases within an European setting, offering guidance for adaptation policies and risk management.

title: Public Support for Universal Road Pricing
affiliations: , Institute of Transport Economics, Oslo and Akershus University College - Oslo Metropolitan University, Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, Institute of Transport Economics and Universidad Complutense de Madrid

detail.title: Public Support for Universal Road Pricing
detail.abstract: Distance-based road pricing can internalize driving externalities and provide fiscally sustainable infrastructure financing as vehicle electrification erodes fuel tax revenues. Yet, political resistance may pose a barrier to implementation. We provide the first comprehensive analysis of preferences for universal road pricing using a stated choice experiment with nearly 4,000 Norwegian respondents. Policy alternatives vary systematically across urban peak prices, off-peak prices, nonurban prices, electric vehicle prices, and revenue allocation. We document robust majority support (70% to 80%) for most universal road pricing schemes, substantially exceeding typical support for local congestion charges. Support varies by design: public transport earmarking outperforms general budget allocation by 8 percentage points, while moderate pricing dominates high pricing by 5 to 7 points. Support varies substantially with car use, availability of transport alternatives, and institutional trust, but shows little sensitivity to income, urban residence, or toll exposure. Latent class analysis identifies unconditional supporters (57%), systematic opponents (22%), and a persuadable middle (21%). Randomized information treatments generate modest effects, with factual information increasing support by 6 percentage points. Political barriers to road pricing may be lower than assumed with moderate pricing and credible infrastructure earmarking.

title: Coal Phase-out in a Second-Best Setting: Evidence from China’s Coal-To-Gas Transition
affiliations: University of Southern California - Sol Price School of Public Policy, World Bank and School of Environment

detail.title: Coal Phase-out in a Second-Best Setting: Evidence from China’s Coal-To-Gas Transition
detail.abstract: As countries phase out coal, natural gas is often promoted as a transitional fuel, but incomplete policies and price distortions can cause emissions leakage, undermining coal reduction efforts. This paper examines China’s 2017 coal-to-gas transition policy, which banned coal in central heating across 28 northern cities, triggering a 70% increase in natural gas prices while coal prices remained stable due to price controls. Using a comprehensive dataset of hourly pollution measures from 1,563 monitors and firm-level data covering around 50% coal consumption in China, we find that instead of reducing coal consumption, the policy led to substantial leakage. Baseline industry composition, the stringency of environmental regulations, and uneven enforcement across polluting firms all contribute to leakage. Back-of-the-envelope calculations suggest that for every ton of coal reduced in the heating sector, coal use increased by 0.53 tons in targeted cities, 1.94 tons in northern non-targeted cities, and 2.30 tons in southern cities. We estimate that 27.9% of the coal consumption rebound could have been prevented if coal prices had been liberalized to fluctuate with natural gas prices, as in European markets. Alternatively, a carbon price of 17 RMB (2.4 USD) per ton of CO2 would achieve an equivalent reduction in coal use while preventing leakage. These findings highlight the importance of addressing market distortions to enhance the effectiveness of coal phase-out policies.

title: U.S. Paris Agreement Exit and Emission Strategy Adjustments
affiliations: VinUniversity

detail.title: U.S. Paris Agreement Exit and Emission Strategy Adjustments
detail.abstract: This paper examines how firms adjust emission strategies when national climate-policy commitment weakens, exploiting the U.S. withdrawal from the Paris Agreement in 2017 as a quasi-natural experiment. Using firm-level data from 2015–2019, I show that U.S. firms reduce their alignment with Paris-consistent emission paths relative to non-U.S. firms, driven by lower emissions-reduction effort—especially in indirect, supply-chain emissions—rather than higher observed pollution. The decline is strongest in high-salience industries, among firms with favorable media sentiment, and those with weaker institutional ownership. Following the withdrawal, Paris alignment is no longer rewarded through ESG ratings, firm performance, or cost of capital, but instead commands an equity return premium. Overall, the findings underscore the importance of policy credibility in sustaining market discipline and firms’ incentives to invest in costly emissions-reduction strategies.

English Abstract: This research aims to analyze the key drivers of inflation in developing countries, with a particular focus on the impact of weak government oversight and the lack of coordination between fiscal and monetary policies. The study introduces a simplified model to explain inflationary dynamics in unstable economies and proposes an institutional framework that assigns part of the price-stability oversight to the central bank to enhance fiscal discipline and reduce inflationary pressures. The model is then applied to a sample of developing countries to validate its explanatory power.

publicationDetails.detailsText: This study forms part of an ongoing macroeconometric working-paper project on the economic impacts of climate-related thermal stress

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the macroeconomic effects of wet-bulb temperature (WBT) shocks in Italy, Spain, Portugal, and Greece, focusing on supply-side transmission channels. Unlike standard 2-meter air temperature, WBT combines heat and humidity and provides a more accurate measure of thermal stress relevant for labor, productivity, and sectoral activity. We employ two complementary Bayesian strategies. In a Bayesian VAR estimated over two subsamples (pre-2012 and post-2012), impulse responses show that in the past decade WBT shocks generate more pronounced contractions in hours worked and industrial production. Forecast error variance decompositions further indicate that the share of macroeconomic variation explained by thermal shocks has increased, underscoring the growing relevance of humid-heat stress in these dynamics. Seasonal Bayesian Local Projections, based on seven sectoral indicators (four price subindices and three activity measures), reveal marked intra-annual heterogeneity: responses are strongest in summer, autumn, and also spring, with price increases and reductions in economic activity across major productive sectors. Overall, the results point to an increasingly important and strongly seasonal role of thermal stress in shaping the economic performance of Southern European countries, with significant implications for labor, production, and price dynamics.

title: Integration of Fiscal and Monetary Policies and the Role of the Central Bank in Achieving Economic Stability: A Proposed Theoretical and Applied Framework
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Integration of Fiscal and Monetary Policies and the Role of the Central Bank in Achieving Economic Stability: A Proposed Theoretical and Applied Framework
detail.abstract: This research aims to analyze the relationship between fiscal and monetary policies and how their integration contributes to achieving economic stability. It introduces a new theoretical and applied framework designed to measure the degree of coordination between these key economic tools in both developed and developing countries. The study highlights the role of the central bank in managing monetary policy and supporting fiscal policy during periods of economic shocks. It also examines the impact of policy integration on inflation, economic growth, and financial stability. The research proposes the “Economic Policy Integration Index,” a quantitative model that assesses the alignment between governmental fiscal decisions and central bank actions. A comparative analysis of real-world cases from Arab and international economies is presented to demonstrate the outcomes of successful policy integration. Finally, the study provides practical recommendations to enhance countries’ ability to navigate crises and achieve sustainable economic stability.

title: Correcting Bias in Estimates of Organic Farming's Economic Viability: Evidence from Structural Causal Models
affiliations: Universidade de Brasília (UnB) and North Carolina State University

detail.title: Correcting Bias in Estimates of Organic Farming's Economic Viability: Evidence from Structural Causal Models
detail.abstract: We reassess the economic viability of organic farming using panel data from Brazilian strawberry smallholders and a structural causal modeling framework. By explicitly quantifying bias in cross-sectional, matching, and fixed-effects models, we show that these approaches systematically overstate benefits and understate costs. Our conditional instrumental variable estimator indicates that organic adoption lowers productivity and profits while raising costs, with price premiums insufficient to offset these disadvantages. Beyond this case, the analysis demonstrates why naïve estimates mislead policy and underscores the need for causal frameworks-echoing EU Green Deal and CAP debates on sustaining adoption through institutional support.

title: Tech vs. Theft: How Smart Traffic Lights Affect Opportunistic Street Crimes

detail.title: Tech vs. Theft: How Smart Traffic Lights Affect Opportunistic Street Crimes
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the unintended consequences of São Paulo's smart traffic signal program on local crime patterns. As part of an infrastructure improvement program in 2023 and 2024, the city replaced traditional traffic lights with smart ones in select areas. Leveraging geolocation data on both crimes and traffic lights, I identify the number of incidents occurring within 100 meters of each traffic signal. By exploiting the staggered implementation of smart traffic lights across different locations, I assess their effect on cell phone thefts and robberies by employing a staggered differencein-differences approach following the methodology of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021). The results reveal a consistent increase in cell phone thefts near treated intersections after smart signals were installed, suggesting a possible unintended consequence of the intervention. Specifically, I find a significant 2.5% monthly increase in cell phone thefts committed from inside vehicles 100 meters near upgraded traffic lights, while cell phone robberies remain unaffected. These findings highlight an important trade-off: although smart technologies can improve urban mobility, policymakers should carefully consider their potential to unintentionally facilitate crime when designing and implementing such interventions.

title: Lawyer Well-Being, Ethics, and the Restorative Power of Pro Bono Service: A Comparative Analysis
affiliations: Delta State University Abraka, Nigeria

detail.title: Lawyer Well-Being, Ethics, and the Restorative Power of Pro Bono Service: A Comparative Analysis
detail.abstract: This article examines the a topic that is rarely talked about in the legal profession. The well-being, ethics, and pro bono culture within the legal profession across the United States, the United Kingdom, and Nigeria. Drawing on global studies, bar association reports, and psychological research, it highlights the profession's mental health crisis and the structural, cultural, and gendered factors that intensify it. It argues that poor well-being undermines individual lawyers, ethical judgment, and institutional performance. Using self-determination theory as a framework, the article explains how autonomy, competence, and relatedness shape lawyer resilience and job satisfaction. It also examines disparities affecting women and underrepresented groups, including harassment, cultural bias, and limited access to mental health resources, especially in developing contexts. The analysis integrates research on the restorative and ethical functions of pro bono work, showing that altruistic service enhances well-being, strengthens professional identity, and supports long-term satisfaction. The article concludes by calling for inclusive work cultures, stronger mental health infrastructure, and global cooperation such as through the IBA Professional Wellbeing Commission to build a healthier and more sustainable legal profession.

title: Understanding the Debt Machine: Who is Borrowing and Why?
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Understanding the Debt Machine: Who is Borrowing and Why?
detail.abstract:
Using aggregate and longitudinal data the research looks at how debt has developed in the UK in the last few decades. It focuses on the factors that have driven changes in household debt using aggregate data. Research in this field has shown factors like interest rates, saving rates, value of financial assets, house prices and age of the population, have been responsible for the change in household debt. Alongside the aggregate data, study also uses UKHLS survey data to divide people into different income groups and look at how debt build-up has differed amongst them and what we can learn from it. Observations from both datasets are compared to see if they are compatible and whether survey data on different income groups helps us to understand change in debt better.

Using the aggregate data, the research finds house prices play a big part in the change in household debt. It also finds deleveraging cycles do not always coincide with low consumption or high savings. The data shows aggregate level of household debt peaked in 2007. Longitudinal survey data also shows debt levels peaked in 2007 for the top 1% and the bottom 10%, but the remaining population has seen its debt consistently increase in the six periods taken between 1995 to 2021.

The aggregate data shows an increase in gross disposable income but using the survey data it can be seen that income growth has been unequal for different income groups. A pattern of decreasing debt for the top 1% can be observed, which has driven the decrease in aggregate debt. This pattern in debt is explained by unequal income growth. It also explains the continued rise in borrowings for the middle-income groups, as these people haven’t seen their income increase as much as the top 1% and have had to borrow to smooth consumption and not fall behind. Thus, looking at the survey data on debt, alongside the aggregate data on household debt provides us with more insight.

title: Credibility, Investment, and Environmental Efficiency: Evidence from Land Use Regulation

detail.title: Credibility, Investment, and Environmental Efficiency: Evidence from Land Use Regulation
detail.abstract: Standard theory treats environmental regulation as a tax on production: restrictions raise costs and reduce output. We document a setting where binding land-use regulation instead engaged a Technique Effect, increasing agricultural investment while reducing pollution. Exploiting the 2005 expansion of Ontario's Greenbelt as a natural experiment, we find that inside the protected area, farmers increased input use (fertilizer application and tile drainage installation) yet water pollution fell by 40-75%. This "Efficiency Wedge" cannot be explained by reduced scale alone; instead it reflects a shift toward cleaner production techniques induced by credible, long-term land protection. These patterns are consistent with investments in modern drainage and precision nutrient management, which improved nutrient uptake efficiency enough to offset higher application rates. Using a spatial regression discontinuity in difference-indifferences design (N = 515,586), we show that securing property rights through regulation led to greater capital investment (notably in drainage infrastructure) and more intensive farming, while pollution concentrations fell-consistent with the resolution of an "impermanence syndrome" whereby insecure tenure had previously discouraged long-term investments. Machine-learning analysis using causal forests and satellite imagery further confirms that benefits were targeted to high-pressure areas and were not driven by pre-existing crop trends. Aggregate agricultural land shares remained stable near the boundary, ruling out compositional shifts as the driver. Our findings demonstrate that when regulation provides credible commitment rather than mere restriction, it can unlock efficiency gains that benefit both farmers and the environment.

title: Neobank and Human Development Index Rise: Evidence from Selected African Countries
affiliations: University of Nigeria - Enugu Campus, University of Nigeria - Enugu Campus, University of Nigeria - Enugu Campus and University of Nigeria

detail.title: Neobank and Human Development Index Rise: Evidence from Selected African Countries
detail.abstract: In recent decades, the economic trajectory in Africa has been characterised by a combination of the negative and positive outcomes with some populations encountering more significant obstacles due to Covid 19 pandemic, while other face comparatively fewer hurdles. The negative risks have resulted in a decline in the Human Development Index, causing policy makers in the area to re evaluate existing programme designed to enhance HDI. This research investigates the ways in which Fintech credits are transforming and enhancing the ahauman development index, especially in regions where banking access is severly limited. The primary concept underlying this observation is that the advent of financial innovation has facilitated the emergence of digital financial services such as NeoBank. These services enables small scale entrepreneurs in the formal sector to avail themselves of financial products and services. It is important to recognise the advantages of theses services extend beyond merely promoting the formalisation and modernisation of the informal economy. They also contribute to the overall improvement of the HDI  and the generation of credit in the unbanked sector of specific African countries, despite its early stage of development where transactions represented less than 1% of the total value from 2017 to 2018 and reached a record high of 2.2% in 2022.

title: Face-to-Face: Confronting Machine-Generated Evidence

detail.title: Face-to-Face: Confronting Machine-Generated Evidence

publicationDetails.detailsText: Fordham Law Legal Studies Research Paper No. 5843422
publicationDetails.journalName: Fordham Law School Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This Note proposes an expanded interpretation of the Sixth Amendment's Confrontation Clause to address challenges presented by machine-generated evidence. Drawing upon the historical concept of "face-to-face" confrontation, including its biblical origins, it argues that the right to confront one's accusers should extend to the algorithms and data underlying machine-generated evidence. The Note develops an analogy between this expanded right and open-source software principles, contending that defendants should be able to examine and challenge the inner workings of machines producing evidence against them. The argument is developed through an analysis of Supreme Court decisions and cases involving machine-generated evidence, paralleling Jacob's transformative wrestling match in Genesis 32:30 to highlight the importance of direct, unmediated confrontation. This includes the right to call expert witnesses to explain and critique machine-generated evidence. Ultimately, this Note aims to preserve meaningful machine confrontation in legal proceedings, thereby ensuring the Confrontation Clause remains relevant and robust.

title: From Acceptance to Aggressive Excellence: Reconstructing Wabi-Sabi, Mono no Aware, and Shame Culture for Competitive Modernity
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: From Acceptance to Aggressive Excellence: Reconstructing Wabi-Sabi, Mono no Aware, and Shame Culture for Competitive Modernity
detail.abstract: Contemporary interpretations of wabi-sabi, mono no aware, and shame culture are argued to have degenerated into justifications for complacency, sentimental inertia, and risk-averse conformity—becoming structural barriers to innovation in modern Japan and beyond. This paper performs a radical reconstruction by fusing these aesthetics with bushidō-derived action imperatives, producing a new practical philosophy labeled Jichū no Dō (“the Way of timely centered advancement”). Core pillars include “impermanence-driven excellence,” “affective fuel,” and “honor through courageous authenticity.” The resulting framework transforms traditional restraints into offensive competitive assets while preserving depth of contemplation.

title: Investment Decision Criteria in Mutual Funds
affiliations: and Universidad Europea de Madrid

detail.title: Investment Decision Criteria in Mutual Funds
detail.abstract: This article examines the variables that determine investment choices in equity mutual funds. It is therefore framed within the nascent discipline of behavioral finance. The study offers a dual perspective by analyzing cash flows and participant flows. Empirical evidence points to past profitability as key in decision-making, while risk loses the interest it had shown in other types of mutual funds. The largest commissions slow the entry of investments, although their effect is dampened as these increase. Other decision variables are also included, such as the size of the fund, the size of the management company, or the overall growth of the investment category. The different results obtained according to the period of expansion or consolidation of the Spanish bond industry, as well as the current state of the markets, demonstrate the need for specific studies of national industries with their own characteristics.

title: A Structural Manifesto of Autonomy: Reconstructing and Anchoring Female Value in Late Capitalism
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: A Structural Manifesto of Autonomy: Reconstructing and Anchoring Female Value in Late Capitalism
detail.abstract: In the era of late capitalism, women confront a distinctive "value vacuum crisis" rooted in structural exploitation: their reproductive labor (including housework, caregiving, and emotional maintenance) is not recognized by the mainstream economic system, while the market substitutes intrinsic value with consumptive symbolic value, triggering widespread value confusion. This paper proposes a philosophical framework for reconstructing women’s value based on three core principles: Structural Recognition, Relational Autonomy, and the Redefinition of Reproductive Value. It further establishes three new functional roles—The Architect (system sovereignty), The Sovereign (emotional self-sufficiency), and The Nexus (high-cost mutual assistance)—and a three-tiered value filtering mechanism (existential/functional value → social relational value → market/symbolic value) to empower women to resist external shocks and construct a self-consistent, structurally stable value system.

title: On the Asymptotic Refinement of Econometric Tests and Estimators in the Normal Linear Regression Model with Non-scalar Error Covariance Matrix
affiliations: and University of Ioannina - Department of Economics

detail.title: On the Asymptotic Refinement of Econometric Tests and Estimators in the Normal Linear Regression Model with Non-scalar Error Covariance Matrix
detail.abstract: In the linear regression model with non-scalar error covariance matrix, y = Xβ+σu; σ > 0; u ∼ NT (0T , Ω-1), where T is the sample size, the second-order asymptotic approximation of the T × T matrix Ω enables the asymptotic refinement of some commonly used econometric tests and estimators in finite samples. The refinement of the t and F econometric tests is asymptotically equivalent to the refinement of the feasible GLS estimators of β and σ 2 , with an error of order O(T-3/2). Therefore, these two refinements can be thought of as alternative remedies to the same problem, that of obtaining valid finite-sample econometric inference.

title: "To Be, or Not to Be (State Resources), That is the Question: AG Spielmann's Opinion in the German KWKG Case (C-242/24 P)"

detail.title: "To Be, or Not to Be (State Resources), That is the Question: AG Spielmann's Opinion in the German KWKG Case (C-242/24 P)"
detail.abstract:
The article outlines how the concept of ‘State resources’ has shaped the boundary between public intervention and private obligations since the PreussenElektra case, and analyses its application to the KWKG system's private financing mechanisms. AG Spielmann’s Opinion  confirms in his Opinion the General Court’s approach in T-409/21, holding that PreussenElektra applies beyond mere price regulation (para. 122). The economic effects of a de-facto levy on the second level (between the TSOs and final consumers) of a triangular relationship are insufficient to constitute a tax, levy or other mandatory surcharge. Consequently, no State resources are involved and therefore no StateAid exists under Article 107(1) TFEU.

This aligns with EEG 2012, in contrast to Vent de Colère, Essent, Achema, FVE Holýšov and Dobeles HES. Yet AG Spielmann leaves a small door open (paras. 123–125) - one that the Court of Justice of the European Union should now close.

title: Exploring the Effect of Oil Prices on Military Spending in the GCC Countries: A New Evidence from PANIC Approach
affiliations: The University of Jordan, Ministry of Finance - General Budget Department ,  and The University of Jordan

detail.title: Exploring the Effect of Oil Prices on Military Spending in the GCC Countries: A New Evidence from PANIC Approach
detail.abstract: This study investigates the effects of oil prices military spending and for a panel of six GCC countries covering the period 1989 to 2021. Unlike most of the previous studies in the field, the study employs the Panel Analysis of Nonstationarity in Idiosyncratic and Common Components approach (PANIC), to deal with complications such as cross-sectional endogeneity, unobserved heterogeneity, and possible non-stationarity. Then the study utilizes also robust econometric techniques namely the Pooled Mean Group (PMG) estimator, which is used to examine the long run and short run connection between the oil prices and military spending, and the Dynamic Common Correlated Effects (DCCE) estimator, which is in turn used to control for cross-sectional dependence with the inclusion of the cross-sectional averages of the dependent and independent variables as additional variables. Findings show that oil prices have a positive and highly significant long-run effect on military expenditure in the GCC countries; a one percentage point increase in oil prices is estimated to lead to a 1.58 percent increase in the percentage of the GDP that is spent on the military. The PMG estimator also reveals that there is a highly significant error correction term, which suggests that the long-term relationships are restored at a rate of 28. 46% per period. The DCCE estimator supports these results, and the PANIC procedure reveals that the idiosyncratic parts of the series are stationary. The economic implications of these findings are examined focusing on the oil-dependent military spending and the probable problem areas include resource distribution, fiscal stability concerns, and the opportunity costs of military expenditure. These findings also show the significance of economic and fiscal transformation and the avoidance of undue dependence on oil revenues in managing the risks that are associated with fluctuations in oil prices on defense expenditure in the GCC states.

title: Environmental Regulation and Urban Energy Security: Evidence from China’s 2017–2018 Air Pollution Control Campaign
affiliations: Beijing Jiaotong University,  and Beijing Jiaotong University

detail.title: Environmental Regulation and Urban Energy Security: Evidence from China’s 2017–2018 Air Pollution Control Campaign
detail.abstract: Whether environmental regulation undermines energy security remains a key question in energy economics, especially in emerging economies facing simultaneous pollution control and energy transitions. This study evaluates the impact of China’s 2017–2018 Autumn and Winter Air Pollution Comprehensive Control Action Plan on urban energy security using a quasi-natural experiment. Employing a Double Machine Learning Difference-in-Differences (DML-DID) framework and panel data from 274 Chinese cities during 2012–2021, we estimate causal effects while addressing high-dimensional confounding. Energy security is measured using a multidimensional index capturing supply adequacy, system reliability, environmental sustainability, and socio-economic acceptability. The results show that the regulation significantly improved overall urban energy security. Importantly, the effect is not driven by an expansion of total energy supply, but by improvements in qualitative dimensions, including infrastructure reliability, environmental performance, and socio-economic acceptance. No significant impact is found on aggregate energy supply. Mechanism analyses indicate that these effects operate through accelerated energy infrastructure upgrading and digital economy development. Heterogeneity analyses further reveal stronger effects in non-resource-based cities, non-old industrial bases, and fiscally unconstrained municipalities. Overall, the findings suggest that well-designed environmental regulation can enhance the quality and resilience of urban energy systems without compromising energy security.

title: Structural Randomness: A Unified Theory
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: Structural Randomness: A Unified Theory
detail.abstract: Many stochastic micro-models admit deterministic macrodynamics once (i) structural constraints restrict admissible laws and (ii) an asymptotic regime yields closure for a projected observable. We formalize this mechanism as a quantitative operator convergence statement on a macro state space (laws, densities, pricing functionals, conditional covariances, or spectral measures). Across canonical settings-central limit renormalization, meanfield particle systems (Vlasov/propagation of chaos), complete markets (Black-Scholes drift elimination), stochastic volatility (deterministic pricing in an enlarged state), linear filtering (path-independent Riccati flow), random matrices (deterministic spectral limits), and neural network training (mean-field limits of gradient descent)-random sample paths coexist with deterministic evolution of the projected object. Talagrand's transportation-cost inequalities provide the quantitative foundation, connecting entropy to Wasserstein geometry and yielding dimension-free concentration bounds that underpin the determinization rates. We also characterize three obstructions: (a) loss of integrability (stable-law regimes), (b) insufficient constraints (set-valued operators in incomplete markets), and (c) ergodicity breaking (path-dependent growth in multiplicative dynamics). The resulting viewpoint treats "probability" as the geometry induced by projection under constraints, and suggests operator-centric diagnostics for model adequacy.

title: Levelized Cost of Political Risk – A new methodological approach for analyzing and managing the risk of renewable energy investments
affiliations: RWTH Aachen University and RWTH Aachen University, University of Siegen - Faculty of Economics and Management Science

detail.title: Levelized Cost of Political Risk – A new methodological approach for analyzing and managing the risk of renewable energy investments
detail.abstract: Green hydrogen is a key enabler for the global energy transition. Due to climate conditions and space limitations, many industrial countries will have to rely on the importing of hydrogen. For this, supply sites in renewable energy-rich countries need to be developed. However, most renewable energy-rich countries are associated with higher level of political risk that can significantly impact production costs. A few studies include country risk in the form of risk-adjusted discount rates as proxy for political risk. However, besides the general drawbacks of using risk-adjusted discount rates, political risk constitutes only a part of overall country risk. The current study bridges this methodological gap through first extending the levelized cost framework by using the certainty equivalent approach to reflect risk in the cash and energy flows instead of the discount rate, and second through incorporating country-specific political risk into a probability-based approach. The applicability of the new method is demonstrated in the use case of green hydrogen production in West Africa. The results indicate that political risk outweighs renewable energy potential for high-risk countries only and increases the cost of green hydrogen production by up to 122.9%. Moreover, political risk may be systematically overestimated when using the prevailing paradigm of adjusting discount rates based on country risk. Nevertheless, strategies such as risk-sharing or transfer mechanisms may improve economic viability. Apart from closing the methodological gap, this study offers a new method for making informed decisions in varying geopolitical contexts and is thus relevant for policymakers and practitioners alike.

detail.abstract: Economic adjustments through trade and migration can mitigate environmental shocks but may also propagate them to other parts of the economy. Using a dynamic spatial general equilibrium model, I quantify the transmission of environmental shocks by capitalizing on the 1930s American Dust Bowl. The local shock in agriculture more than proportionally transmitted to the nontradable sector, while the tradable sector mitigated the shock. Such a disparity hindered structural change. Moreover, the Dust Bowl region exported price increases in subsistence goods, leading to a sizeable welfare loss in the non-Dust Bowl region despite the rises in real income from competition effects.

title: On Options-Driven Realized Volatility Forecasting: Information Gains via Rough Volatility Model
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST), Songhe Chuangzhi Venture Capital and

detail.title: On Options-Driven Realized Volatility Forecasting: Information Gains via Rough Volatility Model
detail.abstract: We examine whether model-based spot volatility estimators extracted from traded options data enhance the predictive power of the Heterogeneous Autoregressive (HAR) model for realized volatility. Specifically, we infer spot volatility under the rough stochastic volatility model via an iterative two-step approach following Andersen et al. (2015a) and adopt a deep learning surrogate to accelerate model estimation from large-scale options panels. Benchmarked against traditional stochastic volatility models (Heston, Bates, SVCJ) and the VIX index, our results demonstrate that the augmented HAR-RV-RHeston model improves daily realized volatility forecasting accuracy and sustains superior performance across horizons up to one month.

detail.abstract: The pricing mechanisms of the digital economy are undergoing a fundamental paradigm shift from human decision-making to algorithmic autonomy. Modern algorithmic pricing systems possess the capability to adjust strategies on a millisecond timescale, presenting a "spiral oscillation" dilemma for traditional antitrust regulation. This paper models the interaction between regulators and algorithms as a strongly-convex-strongly-concave Min-Max game. Through spectral analysis, we uncover the mathematical mechanism whereby traditional "reactive regulation" falls into stagnation due to the indefiniteness of the system's Hessian matrix. Drawing inspiration from recent advances in non-convex optimization (Liu & Luo, 2022), we propose an adversarial regulatory mechanism based on "Hessian-Squared Estimation." Theoretical analysis and simulation experiments demonstrate that this mechanism achieves super-linear convergence independent of the problem's condition number by actively accumulating second-order information via stress testing. Furthermore, we propose an "Algorithmic Audit Sandbox" framework and a novel legal metric termed "Sensitivity Variance" (SV), providing an actionable technical foundation for future antitrust enforcement.

title: Interpretation Nudges and Self-Control

detail.title: Interpretation Nudges and Self-Control
detail.abstract: This paper studies interpretation nudges: interventions that cannot change an objectively generated signal but offer alternative statistical models for interpreting its realizations. Present-biased decision makers select from a menu the model that maximizes statistical fit to the signal realization at their prior, update beliefs, and then decide whether to abstain from a vicious good. I study menu design under asymmetric paternalistic no-harm constraints. In a three-model menu with a binary signal space, I characterize prior-relative no-harm and show that baseline-relative no-harm reduces to a finite check over priors. I then develop an operational search procedure for welfare-improving interpretation nudges within a family of conflicting models. A numerical example illustrates when extreme narratives crowd out welfare-improving abstention and how the conflicting-models search yields pointwise no-harm improvements.

title: Studentized bootstrap confidence intervals for regression parameters under multiple testing

detail.title: Studentized bootstrap confidence intervals for regression parameters under multiple testing
detail.abstract: Suppose a large number of regression models, each with a different response variable but the same set of explanatory variables, are estimated simultaneously. This article develops a new method to simulate confidence intervals for the regression parameters that adjusts for multiple testing and whose coverage achieves second-order accuracy under a reasonable set of assumptions. The method is demonstrated by evaluating the performance of a selection of Australian equity mutual funds. Additionally, new 'multiple-testing-adjusted' performance measures are introduced to evaluate fund manager skill.

title: Why the AI Boom Shows the Signs of a Tech Bubble
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Why the AI Boom Shows the Signs of a Tech Bubble
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of AI investments has raised concerns about the stability and financial sustainability of the sector. This paper examines whether the AI boom shows signs of a tech bubble. Using a microeconomic and macroeconomic approach, the analysis focuses on scaling limits, capital flows, market concentration, energy costs, and supply-chain dependencies. Findings indicate prominent systemic fragility driven by unsustainable capex growth, venture capital misallocation, overly concentrated value chains, runaway growth in energy demand, and geopolitical bottlenecks. The results suggest that the AI sector has embryonic bubble dynamics and highlight areas where practices can be implemented to prevent severe corrections.

title: Euler’s Formula as the Universal Geometric Radar of Systemic Destabilization
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Euler’s Formula as the Universal Geometric Radar of Systemic Destabilization
detail.abstract: A Generalization Beyond Finance  the complex exponential Z(t) = A•e^((γ-ζ + iω)t + iϕ₀) and its associated logarithmic spiral in the complex plane provide a mathematically minimal and empirically superior representation of credit-driven economies (2024-2025) is not an isolated financial curiosity. We show that Euler's formula operates as a **universal geometric early-warning detector** for any system in which a physically constrained "real" component coexists with an expectation-driven, belief-dependent "imaginary" component that can temporarily detach from material limits. The angle θ(t) = arctan(Imaginary / Real) emerges as a **dimensionless, field-invariant fragility indicator** that consistently signals impending corrective crises when it crosses the narrow band 42°-50°. We demonstrate the identical spiral geometry and critical-angle threshold in financial leverage, mass migration and social cohesion, type-2 diabetes epidemics, higher-education debt bubbles, and climate-policy credibility gaps. The scientific community has not yet widely recognized this unification; the present paper calls for the immediate creation of an interdisciplinary "Complex Fragility" research program.

title: A Sustainability Assessment of Single-Use Plastics Regulation in Costa Rica

detail.title: A Sustainability Assessment of Single-Use Plastics Regulation in Costa Rica

detail.abstract: Over the last decade, as the effects of climate change have become increasingly evident through scientific findings and heightened public awareness, governments worldwide have introduced regulations to curb the environmental harm caused by single-use plastics. Costa Rica is one such country. Long recognized for its progressive achievements in environmental conservation, biodiversity protection, and the advancement of nature rights, Costa Rica has established itself as a global environmental leader. In line with this leadership, the country has set an ambitious goal to completely eliminate single-use plastics and have zero plastic waste. Effective regulation of plastics and other environmentally harmful materials represents a critical benchmark in Costa Rica’s national environmental policy agenda, as well as its commitment to multilateral agreements aimed at addressing climate change and promoting sustainability. This paper presents a sustainability assessment of Costa Rica’s regulation of single-use plastics, examining the country’s experiences and approaches in advancing this policy objective.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Flow Accounting System (FAS), a single-flow, event-based measurement framework that replaces the debit-credit mechanics of traditional double-entry bookkeeping. FAS proposes a Minimum Five-Flow Taxonomy (M5F)-Resource Flow, Value Flow, Claim Flow, Equity Flow, and Adjustment Flow-representing the smallest complete set of flow categories required to capture all accounting-relevant economic events. Unlike ledger-based systems, FAS operates as a state-computation model, where all financial statements emerge automatically from the aggregation of flows into the State of Assets (SOA), State of Obligations (SOO), and Net Worth.

The model provides a mathematically complete and operationally simpler alternative to legacy accounting structures. It eliminates the cognitive burden of debit-credit classification, supports automated processing, and aligns naturally with modern digital infrastructures such as ERP systems, APIs, blockchain, and event-driven architectures. The five-flow minimum structure offers conceptual parsimony, while its enterprise extension—the twelve-flow taxonomy—supports granular representation without compromising coherence.

A detailed worked example demonstrates that FAS produces the same measurement results as double-entry while significantly reducing complexity. The framework enables real-time reporting, continuous auditing, and seamless integration with intelligent systems. This paper positions FAS as a practical and theoretically grounded foundation for modern financial reporting in a digitally automated economy.

title: Impact of Privatization on Quality Education in the Indian Society

detail.title: Impact of Privatization on Quality Education in the Indian Society
detail.abstract: Education is the base of the society and without it we cannot assume development of the society. The importance of education is rising day by day. Technological advances, modern life standards require well educated, proficient people around the world. Moreover, education is seen as an important tool to reach economic achievement for the countries. Hence, many governments try to succeed in the education sector, by trying to develop it. Indian government has also taken many steps regarding development of the education, among these steps privatization is the major step which is taken in the 1991. Privatization has brought about rapid change in the educational scenario of India. It is seen that privatization encourages the individuals and religious organizations to establish colleges and deemed universities to meet the growing demand for higher education. Consequently, higher educational institutions are found throughout the country. It not only increases the number of higher educational institutions but also increases the number of seats for highly demand courses such as engineering and medicine. Moreover, it decreases the distance between the educational institutions. It causes competition among them to fill the seats allotted by the affiliated universities and maximize socio- economic benefits. However, it creates the gap between the demand and supply of higher education. It not only increases the cost but also decreases the quality of education. Thus, privatization has positive and negative impact on education and society. Hence, this paper examines privatization in education and its impact on education quality in the Indian society at micro level.

detail.abstract: In July 2021, the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) officially classified Korea as a developed country. This marked a remarkable transformation for a nation that was once among the poorest in the world, grappling with the devastation of the Korean War in 1950. Through rapid industrialization and democratization, Korea successfully ascended to developed status. Ranked among the world's top 10 trading nations, Korea surpassed Japan in 2024, reaching a per capita Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of 36,000 USD. In addition, Korea has also successfully reforested its once-devastated land, enabling its people to enjoy a rich natural environment, healthy lifestyles, and a high standard of welfare. In 1982, the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) highlighted Korea’s reforestation in its report called Village Forestry Development in the Republic of Korea. The FAO praised Korea as “the only developing country to have succeeded in reforestation since World War II.” This statement remains valid today, as reforestation in developing countries is still considered more difficult than industrialization. Lester R. Brown, founder of the Earth Policy Institute in the United States, wrote in his book Plan B 2.0: Rescuing a Planet Under Stress and a Civilization in Trouble that “Korea is in many ways a model for global reforestation... We too can make the planet green again.” Although reforestation is widely recognized in Korea as a successful case, there has been a lack of research on the specific processes that led to this achievement. As a result, many citizens remain unaware of how reforestation was accomplished. Some mistakenly believe that forests simply regenerated on their own as rural populations declined and fossil fuels replaced traditional forest fuels. However, barren lands devoid of even a single blade of grass or tree cannot be restored unless humans intentionally introduce vegetation from external sources. This study aims to correct such misconceptions, properly recognize the efforts of earlier generations who restored the devastated land into today’s lush green mountains, and explore the key factors behind the rapid national reforestation. In particular, it focuses on the administrative and policy strategies, especially the regulation of widespread slash-and-burn cultivation that contributed to the success of Korea’s forest restoration.

title: Becoming Co-ed: a Protestant Gift to China
affiliations: Jinan University, Peking University - Guanghua School of Management and Peking University, School of Economics

detail.title: Becoming Co-ed: a Protestant Gift to China
detail.abstract: Until the arrival of Protestant missionaries in the 19th century, women in China had little access to formal education. The Protestant missionaries built the first school, the first college, and the first medical school that admitted women, thereby opening up womens pathways to higher education and professional services. Using various measures of Protes- tant activities by 1920 and college yearbooks published in 1928-1935, we find that the Protestant missions exerted significant impact on narrowing gender inequality in higher education. We suggest that this effect came through two channels: providing women- inclusive secondary education and affecting norms among their converts. Additionally, we find that the increase in educational attainment led to a higher number of female doctors and civil servants in the short run and a higher gender ratio in skilled occupations in the long run.

detail.abstract: Bangladesh's health sector faces persistent and deeply rooted challenges, including weak governance, shortage of skilled workforce, inadequate financing, mismanagement of resources, and poor quality of service delivery. Despite notable improvements in maternal and child health indicators over the past decades, the system continues to experience inefficiencies that undermine progress. This article explores these systemic challenges by applying a management point of view, drawing insights from the works of Khaled (2025), who emphasizes the role of strategic planning, institutional discipline, leadership capability, and organizational efficiency in improving government sectors. In addition to identifying major problems, this paper presents a management-oriented roadmap for sustainable health sector reform in Bangladesh. The recommendations are based on practical experiences, academic research, and lessons from public sector management perspectives. By integrating management principles such as accountability, strategic vision, human resource development, and technological innovation, the article aims to offer a structured, implementable solution for strengthening the health system. The expected outcomes include improved service delivery, enhanced governance structures, efficient resource utilization, and greater trust in public healthcare institutions.
